model.name: NHS England As-Is Enterprise Architecture
model.documentation: An as-is ArchiMate model of the health service in England as commissioned, funded and overseen nationally. Contains a hierarchical business capability model, value streams, key business processes, a conceptual information model, stakeholders, application services and named information flows, with the relationships between them. Recorded in August 2026, while NHS England is being wound down into the Department of Health and Social Care, integrated care board boundaries are changing and national running costs are being halved. Statements about where accountability sits are therefore provisional by construction.

element.name: Care Delivery Capabilities
element.documentation: The abilities through which care is actually delivered to people. Almost none of them are exercised by the national body: they are exercised by around 200 trusts, roughly 6,000 general practices operating as independent contractors, community and mental health providers, community pharmacy and a substantial independent sector. The national enterprise commissions, funds, standardises and holds to account, which means its influence over delivery runs through contract, standard, payment and inspection rather than through line management. Understanding that is the single most important thing about this architecture: the centre does not operate the service it is accountable for.

property.value: Provider trusts; foundation trusts; primary medical contractors; community and mental health providers; independent sector

element.name: Urgent and Emergency Care
element.documentation: The ability to receive, triage and treat unscheduled need across a tiered system running from digital and telephone triage through urgent treatment centres and same day emergency care to emergency departments and ambulance conveyance. The capability is the most visible measure of system health and the least controllable by any single organisation, because performance in emergency departments is determined largely by flow conditions elsewhere: bed occupancy, discharge readiness, community capacity and social care availability. Demand arrives through several front doors operating on different clinical records, so the same person may be triaged more than once with no shared account of what has already been decided.

property.value: Acute trusts; ambulance trusts; NHS 111 providers; urgent treatment centres; primary care out of hours

element.name: Telephone and Digital Triage
element.documentation: Assessing need remotely and directing to the appropriate service or self care. Volume is very large and disposition accuracy determines downstream load, so small changes in triage behaviour move demand across the whole urgent care system.

element.name: Ambulance Response and Pre-Hospital Care
element.documentation: Call categorisation, dispatch, treatment at scene and conveyance decisions. Pre-hospital clinical records reach receiving hospitals inconsistently, so handover is substantially verbal and the trajectory before arrival is frequently reduced to a summary sentence.

element.name: Emergency Department and Same Day Emergency Care
element.documentation: Assessment, treatment and disposition for people attending in person, including admission avoidance through same day pathways. Constrained at the exit rather than the entrance.

element.name: Urgent Community Response
element.documentation: Responding within hours to a crisis in a person's own residence to avoid conveyance and admission. Effective and dependent on capacity that is unevenly distributed and rarely visible in real time to the services that would refer into it.

element.name: Planned and Elective Care
element.documentation: The ability to deliver referred, scheduled care from outpatient assessment through diagnostics to procedure and follow-up. The capability carrying the largest single accountability pressure in the system, since elective waiting is the most politically salient measure the enterprise reports. It is also the capability most exposed to the separation between demand and capacity: referrals are generated by independent primary medical contractors, capacity is held by trusts and independent providers, and neither party sees the other's position without a national or regional intermediary. Independent sector capacity is used at scale, and episodes delivered there return as correspondence rather than as records.

property.value: Acute and specialist trusts; independent sector providers; specialised commissioning

element.name: Outpatient Assessment and Follow-Up
element.documentation: First and follow-up consultation, increasingly with advice and guidance substituting for referral and with patient-initiated follow-up replacing routine review. High volume, comparatively weakly coded, and the principal site of elective demand.

element.name: Surgical and Procedural Care
element.documentation: Theatre and procedural delivery including day case and high volume low complexity pathways in dedicated hubs. Productivity is measured centrally and determined locally by scheduling, workforce and estate.

property.value: Acute trusts; surgical hubs; independent sector

element.name: Specialised and Highly Specialised Services
element.documentation: Low volume, high complexity services commissioned nationally or through provider collaboratives against national service specifications. The clearest example of national commissioning acting directly on delivery.

property.value: Specialist centres; national commissioning; provider collaboratives

element.name: Primary Medical Care
element.documentation: The ability to provide first contact, continuing, comprehensive and coordinated medical care to a registered population. Structurally distinctive and architecturally decisive: general practice is delivered by independent businesses holding contracts, using clinical systems the NHS does not own, and holding the most complete longitudinal record of the population that exists anywhere in the system. Registration creates the list against which nearly all population accountability is calculated. The national enterprise influences primary medical care through the contract, the network arrangement, incentive schemes and system supplier assurance rather than through direction, which is why change here takes contract cycles rather than management decisions.

property.value: General practices as independent contractors; primary care networks; ICB primary care commissioning

element.name: Registration and List Management
element.documentation: Maintaining the registered list, which is the denominator for capitation, incentive schemes, screening invitation and most population reporting. List accuracy is a systemic dependency and a recognised data quality problem.

element.name: Consultation and Continuing Care
element.documentation: Assessment, diagnosis, treatment and continuity across episodes, in person, by telephone and online. The record produced here is the closest thing the system has to a longitudinal account of a person.

element.name: Long-Term Condition Review and Recall
element.documentation: Structured recall and review for people with long-term conditions, driven substantially by incentive scheme definitions. Among the best structured clinical data in the system and largely invisible outside the practice.

element.name: Enhanced and Network Services
element.documentation: Services delivered above the core contract through network arrangements and enhanced services, including additional roles and neighbourhood working. The layer currently subject to contracting reform.

property.value: Primary care networks; general practices; community pharmacy

element.name: Community and Intermediate Care
element.documentation: The ability to deliver nursing, therapy, rehabilitation and reablement in people's homes and in community settings, and to support discharge from hospital. The capability on which flow through the acute sector depends and the one with the weakest information infrastructure: community activity is recorded in systems that vary widely, returns to national datasets less completely than acute activity, and interacts constantly with local authority social care under separate statutory accountability and separate funding. Delayed discharge is the visible symptom of a capability boundary that no single organisation controls.

property.value: Community trusts; social enterprises; local authorities; voluntary sector; intermediate care services

element.name: Community Nursing and Therapy
element.documentation: District nursing, specialist nursing and allied health delivery in home and clinic settings. Caseload rather than episode shaped, which fits national activity reporting poorly.

element.name: Intermediate Care and Reablement
element.documentation: Short-term support to recover function after illness or admission. Jointly funded and jointly delivered, and therefore jointly accountable in a way that complicates both measurement and improvement.

property.value: Community providers; local authorities; intermediate care beds

element.name: Discharge Coordination and Transfer of Care
element.documentation: Planning and effecting discharge, including onward packages of care. The highest-friction interface in the system, and the point where health and social care accountability meet without a shared record.

property.value: Acute trusts; community providers; local authorities; transfer of care hubs

element.name: Mental Health Care
element.documentation: The ability to assess, treat and support people with mental illness across community teams, talking therapy services, crisis response, inpatient care and specialised provision, including care delivered under the Mental Health Act. The record here is predominantly narrative, the statutory layer runs in parallel to the clinical account on its own legal timetable, and out of area placement remains a persistent feature where local capacity is unavailable. Waiting time measurement is less mature than in physical health, so the capability is systematically less visible in national reporting than its share of need would imply.

property.value: Mental health trusts; primary care; voluntary sector; crisis services; specialised commissioning

element.name: Community Mental Health and Talking Therapies
element.documentation: Assessment, therapy and continuing support in community settings, including the high volume talking therapy programme which is among the best measured services in the sector.

property.value: Mental health trusts; talking therapy services; primary care

element.name: Crisis Response and Liaison
element.documentation: Urgent mental health response, including crisis lines, liaison in emergency departments and joint working with police under place of safety arrangements.

property.value: Crisis teams; liaison psychiatry; ambulance and police interfaces

element.name: Inpatient and Statutory Mental Health Care
element.documentation: Admission, including detention under the Mental Health Act, with statutory documentation, tribunal review and out of area placement where local beds are unavailable.

property.value: Mental health trusts; independent providers; Mental Health Act administration

element.name: Children and Young People's Mental Health
element.documentation: Assessment and treatment for children and young people, with transition to adult services at an age boundary that changes provider, record and frequently threshold at the same moment.

property.value: Mental health trusts; schools; local authorities

element.name: Maternity and Neonatal Care
element.documentation: The ability to care for women and birthing people through pregnancy, birth and the postnatal period, and for newborns requiring specialist care. Distinctive in being a continuous surveillance relationship over many months rather than a sequence of episodes, and in producing two linked records from a single event. The capability has been the subject of sustained national scrutiny and improvement programmes following repeated service failures, which makes its data and its escalation routes unusually heavily specified compared with adjacent capabilities.

property.value: Acute trusts; community midwifery; neonatal networks; local maternity and neonatal systems

element.name: Antenatal Care and Risk Assessment
element.documentation: Booking, continuing surveillance and risk stratification across pregnancy, with pathway allocation revised as risk changes. Provisional by design, and the current classification is reliably known only to the team holding the woman.

element.name: Intrapartum Care
element.documentation: Care during labour and birth across settings, including transfer between them. Real-time availability of the clinical picture is a safety property in this capability rather than a convenience.

property.value: Obstetric units; midwifery led units; home birth services

element.name: Neonatal and Postnatal Care
element.documentation: Care of the newborn including specialist neonatal levels, and postnatal care of mother and baby. The point at which one clinical event becomes two longitudinal records whose linkage is maintained largely by practice.

property.value: Neonatal units and networks; community midwifery; health visiting

element.name: Diagnostics and Pathology
element.documentation: The ability to convert a clinical question into a test, perform it and return an interpreted result. Consolidating into pathology networks and imaging networks and into community diagnostic centres intended to separate elective diagnostics from acute pressure. Imaging behaves as a retrieval capability where shared archives exist and as a transmission capability where they do not; pathology remains substantially a transmission capability in which results are delivered to a requester and comparability between laboratories depends on local codes and reference ranges that networking is progressively standardising.

property.value: Acute trusts; pathology networks; community diagnostic centres; imaging networks

element.name: Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
element.documentation: Specimen receipt, analysis, validation and reporting across networked laboratories. Consolidation is a semantic programme as much as an operational one.

element.name: Imaging and Radiology
element.documentation: Acquisition, reporting and distribution of imaging, with reporting capacity a national constraint and cross-site image sharing dependent on shared archive arrangements.

property.value: Acute trusts; imaging networks; community diagnostic centres

element.name: Physiological and Endoscopic Diagnostics
element.documentation: Endoscopy, cardiorespiratory and other physiological measurement. Capacity constrained by workforce and estate more than by equipment.

element.name: Genomic Testing
element.documentation: Testing delivered through a national genomic medicine service against a national test directory. Unusual in being nationally specified at the level of which test may be ordered for which indication.

property.value: Genomic laboratory hubs; clinical genetics services

element.name: Medicines Optimisation and Pharmacy
element.documentation: The ability to prescribe, supply, review and pay for medicines safely and affordably. The prescribing side is substantially digital in primary care through electronic prescription transmission, which is one of the few genuinely national end-to-end digital flows in the system. The hospital and community boundary remains weaker, reconciliation at transitions is a repeated manual control, and the commercial function negotiating price and access operates at national scale with direct effect on what may be prescribed locally.

property.value: Community pharmacy; hospital pharmacy; primary care; national commercial medicines function

element.name: Prescribing and Electronic Prescription Transmission
element.documentation: Generating and transmitting prescriptions electronically from prescriber to dispenser. Mature in primary care and less complete across secondary and community boundaries.

property.value: General practices; prescribers; national prescription service

element.name: Dispensing and Community Pharmacy Services
element.documentation: Supply, clinical check and an expanding set of clinical services delivered under the pharmacy contract, including consultation and treatment for defined conditions.

element.name: Medicines Reconciliation and Review
element.documentation: Establishing what a person is actually taking at transitions and reviewing appropriateness. A compensating control repeated at each transition because no system holds an authoritative current list.

property.value: Hospital pharmacy; primary care pharmacy teams

element.name: Commercial Medicines and Access Management
element.documentation: Negotiating price and access, and implementing funding decisions arising from technology appraisal. Acts upstream of the clinical encounter and constrains it nationally.

property.value: National commercial function; technology appraisal bodies

element.name: Population and Prevention Capabilities
element.documentation: The abilities directed at populations rather than at presenting individuals. Structurally split across organisational boundaries that do not align: health protection sits with a separate national agency, local public health sits with local government, screening and immunisation programmes are commissioned nationally and delivered through primary care and providers, and population health analysis sits with integrated care boards and the national centre. The split is a legacy of successive reorganisations rather than a design, and it means population capability requires coordination across statutory bodies with different accountabilities.

property.value: National public health functions; UKHSA; local authority public health; ICBs; screening and immunisation programmes

element.name: Population Health Management
element.documentation: The ability to understand the health needs, risks and inequalities of a defined population and to act on that understanding through targeted intervention. Requires linked longitudinal data across primary care, secondary care, community, mental health and increasingly social care. The linkage exists in national and regional analytic environments rather than in the operational estate, so insight is generated at a distance from the teams expected to act on it and must be pushed back to them as lists and dashboards.

property.value: ICBs; provider collaboratives; national analytics; primary care networks

element.name: Segmentation and Risk Stratification
element.documentation: Dividing a population by need and identifying those at rising risk. Methodologically variable between systems, which limits comparability of the interventions built on it.

property.value: ICB analytics; national analytics; primary care networks

element.name: Case Finding and Proactive Outreach
element.documentation: Identifying and contacting people who would benefit from intervention before they present. Depends on list accuracy and on capacity to act once someone is found.

element.name: Population Segment Service Design
element.documentation: Designing offers around defined population segments rather than around existing service boundaries. The intent behind neighbourhood and integrated care policy.

element.name: Screening and Immunisation
element.documentation: The ability to invite, test, vaccinate, recall and follow up defined populations against national programme specifications. Programmes operate their own call and recall infrastructure derived from registration data rather than from clinical systems, which makes them message-connected to care rather than integrated with it. Failsafe recall is one of the few genuinely closed loops in the enterprise, and it is closed inside the programme rather than across the wider system, which is both its strength and the reason programme boundaries are a recurring source of incident.

property.value: National programmes; primary care; provider trusts; UKHSA

element.name: Screening Programme Delivery
element.documentation: Invitation, testing, result management and referral into diagnostic pathways for the national programmes. Failsafe integrity is the defining safety obligation.

property.value: National screening programmes; providers; primary care

element.name: Immunisation Delivery and Coverage
element.documentation: Delivering and recording vaccination across life stages and reporting coverage. Records are distributed across practice systems and national services, so a complete history requires reconciliation.

property.value: Primary care; school age services; community pharmacy; UKHSA

element.name: Health Protection and Emergency Preparedness
element.documentation: The ability to detect and respond to communicable disease, environmental hazards and major incidents, and to maintain preparedness for them. Held jointly with a separate national agency and with local resilience structures, exercised through statutory notification, surveillance and command arrangements that activate rarely and must work immediately when they do. The pandemic demonstrated both the reach of this capability and its dependence on data flows assembled under pressure rather than maintained in readiness.

property.value: UKHSA; NHS England emergency preparedness; providers; local resilience forums

element.name: Communicable Disease Surveillance and Response
element.documentation: Notification, investigation and outbreak management, dependent on consistent laboratory coding across contributing sources.

element.name: Emergency Preparedness, Resilience and Response
element.documentation: Planning for and commanding the response to major incidents, including surge and mutual aid across organisational boundaries.

property.value: NHS England and successor arrangements; providers; local resilience forums

element.name: Health Inequalities and Prevention
element.documentation: The ability to identify and reduce differences in access, experience and outcome between groups, and to intervene before need becomes demand. The capability most dependent on parties the NHS does not commission, since the determinants of the outcomes it targets sit largely in housing, income, education and environment. It is measured through national frameworks and delivered through local partnership, which makes attribution of effect genuinely difficult and makes the capability vulnerable when financial pressure forces prioritisation toward measurable short-term delivery.

property.value: ICBs; local authorities; providers; national policy functions

element.name: Inequalities Measurement and Targeting
element.documentation: Measuring differential access and outcome and directing resource accordingly, against national frameworks for reducing inequality.

property.value: ICB and national analytics; local authorities

element.name: Prevention and Behavioural Intervention
element.documentation: Delivering secondary prevention and behaviour change programmes, including national diabetes prevention and smoking cessation offers.

element.name: Access and Flow Capabilities
element.documentation: The abilities that determine whether a person can get into the service they need and move through it. These are the capabilities on which the enterprise is publicly judged, and they are exercised across organisational boundaries by design: referral is generated in one organisation and received in another, capacity is held by several, and the person's position in a queue is a national statistic assembled from local lists. Access management is therefore an information capability at least as much as an operational one.

property.value: ICBs; providers; national access functions; independent sector

element.name: Access, Referral and Booking
element.documentation: The ability to convert a clinical decision to refer into a booked appointment with an appropriate provider. Supported by a national electronic referral service that carries most consultant-led referral and by advice and guidance routes that increasingly divert referral before it is made. The capability is where patient choice becomes operational, and where the mismatch between where demand arises and where capacity sits is first visible. Referral triage outcomes return to the referrer inconsistently, so a general practitioner does not reliably learn what happened to a referral they made.

property.value: General practices; acute trusts; national e-referral service; independent sector

element.name: Referral Generation and Advice and Guidance
element.documentation: Making a referral or seeking specialist advice without one. Advice and guidance is now a substantial diversion route and changes the demand profile reaching outpatients.

element.name: Electronic Referral and Booking
element.documentation: Directory-based referral, slot publication and booking, including patient-initiated booking. One of the longest-established national digital services.

property.value: National e-referral service; providers; primary care

element.name: Referral Triage and Vetting
element.documentation: Clinical assessment of referral appropriateness and priority, performed on the referral document rather than on a record.

element.name: Patient Flow and Capacity Management
element.documentation: The ability to match demand to capacity in real time across beds, theatres, clinics, ambulances and community capacity. Exercised largely within organisations, with system-level coordination through operational pressure escalation arrangements that activate when local capacity fails. There is no single view of capacity across a system, so mutual aid and diversion decisions rest on telephone contact and periodic situation reporting rather than on shared operational data.

property.value: Acute trusts; ambulance trusts; ICBs; regional operations

element.name: Bed and Site Management
element.documentation: Managing occupancy, admission from the emergency department and internal transfer. Constrained at the discharge boundary rather than the admission one.

element.name: Theatre and Clinic Utilisation
element.documentation: Scheduling and using elective capacity efficiently. Measured nationally and determined by local scheduling practice, which limits comparability.

element.name: System Escalation and Mutual Aid
element.documentation: Coordinating response when local capacity is exceeded, through defined escalation levels and mutual aid between providers.

element.name: Waiting List and Elective Recovery Management
element.documentation: The ability to hold, validate, prioritise and reduce lists of people waiting for care. Lists are maintained per provider and per specialty, so the national waiting position is an aggregation of locally maintained lists rather than a view of a single queue. Validation materially affects reported performance, which makes validation practice itself a governance concern. Mutual aid, independent sector capacity and patient-initiated transfer are the principal levers for moving demand to where capacity exists.

property.value: Providers; ICBs; national access functions; independent sector

element.name: Waiting List Maintenance and Validation
element.documentation: Keeping lists accurate, removing entries no longer required and confirming that people still want and need treatment. Directly affects the reported position.

element.name: Clinical Prioritisation
element.documentation: Assigning and revising clinical priority so that waiting is ordered by need rather than only by duration.

element.name: Capacity Purchasing and Transfer
element.documentation: Commissioning additional capacity and transferring people to providers with availability, including into the independent sector.

element.name: Patient Choice and Digital Access
element.documentation: The ability of people to see, choose and transact with services directly, through the national patient application, online consultation tools and provider portals. Increasingly the front door of the system and an aggregation layer rather than an integration one: what a citizen sees is assembled from sources of varying completeness, so the quality of the citizen's view is a direct reflection of the architecture behind it.

property.value: National digital services; providers; primary care

element.name: Citizen Digital Channel Operation
element.documentation: Operating the national patient-facing application and website, including record access, appointment management and prescription ordering.

element.name: Online Consultation and Digital Front Door
element.documentation: Receiving and triaging requests submitted online, and managing total demand across channels.

element.name: Choice and Provider Information
element.documentation: Publishing comparable information about providers and waiting times so that choice is informed rather than nominal.

element.name: Commissioning and System Management Capabilities
element.documentation: The abilities by which the enterprise decides what to buy, from whom, at what price, and whether it was delivered. These are the capabilities most directly affected by the current restructure: functions are moving from the national body into the department, regional teams are becoming departmental outposts, integrated care board boundaries changed in April 2026 with further change due in April 2027, and running cost reductions are being applied across all of them simultaneously. Capability continuity through that transition is a live architectural risk rather than a theoretical one.

property.value: DHSC; NHS England in transition; ICBs; regional teams; provider collaboratives

element.name: Strategic Commissioning and Planning
element.documentation: The ability to determine what services a population needs, plan their provision and allocate resource accordingly. Held principally by integrated care boards for their populations, within national planning guidance and financial allocation set centrally, and informed by joint strategic needs assessment with local government. The reduction in commissioner running costs and the consolidation of integrated care board footprints are simultaneously reducing the capacity to exercise this capability and increasing the population each commissioner must exercise it over.

property.value: ICBs; DHSC and NHS England in transition; integrated care partnerships; local authorities

element.name: Needs Assessment and Strategy
element.documentation: Establishing population need and setting an integrated care strategy with partners, including the local authority statutory contribution.

property.value: ICBs; integrated care partnerships; local authorities

element.name: Operational and Financial Planning
element.documentation: Converting national planning guidance and allocation into annual operational plans with activity, workforce and financial trajectories.

element.name: Service Change and Reconfiguration
element.documentation: Changing where and how services are delivered, subject to consultation and scrutiny requirements that set the pace independently of clinical or financial logic.

element.name: Contracting and Provider Payment
element.documentation: The ability to convert a commissioning intention into a binding contract and to pay against it. Runs through several distinct instruments that behave differently: the national standard contract with trusts, nationally negotiated contracts with primary medical and pharmacy contractors, network arrangements, and procurement under the provider selection regime. Payment mixes block and aligned payment arrangements with activity-based elements and incentive schemes, so the relationship between what is delivered and what is paid is indirect and reconciled after the event.

property.value: ICBs; national contracting functions; providers; primary care contractors

element.name: NHS Standard Contract Management
element.documentation: Issuing, varying and managing the national standard contract, including its information and quality requirements.

element.name: Primary Care and Pharmacy Contracting
element.documentation: Managing nationally negotiated contracts with independent primary medical, pharmacy, dental and optical contractors, and the enhanced services above them.

element.name: Payment, Pricing and Incentives
element.documentation: Applying the national tariff and payment scheme, aligned payment arrangements and incentive schemes, and reconciling activity to payment.

element.name: Procurement and Provider Selection
element.documentation: Selecting providers under the applicable regime, including direct award and competitive routes.

element.name: Performance and Oversight
element.documentation: The ability to see how the system is performing and to intervene where it is not. Exercised through a national oversight framework with segmentation of organisations by level of support required, through regional teams holding providers and commissioners to account, and through statutory regulation by a separate inspectorate. The information underpinning it is assembled retrospectively from national datasets and returns rather than observed operationally, so oversight sees the system as a sequence of periodic snapshots and intervenes after the fact.

property.value: DHSC; NHS England in transition; regional teams; ICBs; CQC

element.name: Oversight Framework and Segmentation
element.documentation: Assessing organisations against the national oversight framework and determining the level of support or intervention required.

element.name: Performance Reporting and Statistics
element.documentation: Producing the published statistics on access, activity, quality and finance, most of which are official statistics with defined publication timetables.

property.value: National statistics and analytics functions; providers

element.name: Intervention and Recovery Support
element.documentation: Providing or imposing support where performance, finance or quality require it, up to and including changes of leadership.

element.name: Financial Management and Allocation
element.documentation: The ability to allocate, control and account for public money across the system. Allocation runs from departmental settlement through weighted capitation to integrated care boards, which then contract with providers. Accountability is statutory and personal: system financial balance is a duty, and the mechanisms for restoring it in year are blunt because activity-linked financial information is retrospective. Capital and revenue operate on different rhythms, which is a persistent constraint on the digital and estate investment the rest of the architecture depends on.

property.value: DHSC; NHS England in transition; ICBs; providers; national finance functions

element.name: Allocation and Financial Framework
element.documentation: Distributing the settlement to systems through weighted capitation and setting the financial framework within which they operate.

element.name: In-Year Financial Control and Reporting
element.documentation: Monitoring position against plan, forecasting and applying corrective control. Monthly cycle, retrospective data.

property.value: ICBs; providers; regional and national finance

element.name: Costing and Efficiency
element.documentation: Collecting patient-level cost data and using it to drive efficiency and pricing. Among the more sophisticated national data collections and among the least used operationally.

element.name: Capital Planning and Investment
element.documentation: Prioritising and approving capital investment including estate and digital. Multi-year cycles that align imperfectly with annual revenue planning.

property.value: DHSC; NHS England in transition; providers

element.name: Workforce Planning and Supply
element.documentation: The ability to plan, train, recruit, retain and deploy the workforce. The largest cost in the system and its principal capacity constraint. Planning runs on a long horizon set by training pipelines while operational pressure runs on an annual one, and the levers available to the centre are education commissioning, national terms and conditions and international recruitment policy rather than deployment. Professional registration sits with independent regulators, so the enterprise consults workforce registers it does not own.

property.value: DHSC; NHS England in transition; providers; education bodies; professional regulators

element.name: Long-Term Workforce Planning
element.documentation: Projecting supply and demand and commissioning training places against it, on a horizon far longer than the financial planning cycle.

element.name: Recruitment, Retention and Deployment
element.documentation: Attracting and keeping staff and deploying them where need is greatest, including temporary staffing and bank and agency management.

element.name: Education, Training and Revalidation
element.documentation: Delivering education and continuing professional development and supporting revalidation against regulator requirements.

element.name: Estates, Procurement and Supply Chain
element.documentation: The ability to provide and maintain the physical estate and to source, buy and distribute the goods the system consumes. Estate condition and maintenance backlog are material constraints on both clinical productivity and digital deployment. Procurement operates through national frameworks and a national supply chain organisation alongside local purchasing, so aggregate spend visibility is better than consumption visibility at the point of use.

property.value: Providers; national supply chain functions; DHSC; commercial partners

element.name: Estates and Facilities Management
element.documentation: Maintaining and developing the estate, managing backlog maintenance and delivering new capacity.

element.name: Procurement and Category Management
element.documentation: Sourcing through national frameworks and local competition, with category strategies for major spend areas.

element.name: Supply Chain and Logistics
element.documentation: Warehousing and distributing consumables and equipment, including resilience against supply disruption.

element.name: Digital, Data and Technology Capabilities
element.documentation: The abilities that create, move, protect and interpret the enterprise's information. England has an unusually strong set of national digital services by international comparison, built up over two decades and consolidated into the national body when the separate digital organisation was absorbed in 2023. The characteristic pattern is national identity, national messaging and national citizen channels sitting above a provider estate of independently procured electronic record systems, with shared care records assembling a view across them rather than replacing them. Those national services are now themselves inside an organisation being dissolved, which places continuity of critical national infrastructure on the transition risk register.

property.value: National digital functions in transition; ICBs; providers; suppliers

element.name: National Digital Service Operation
element.documentation: The ability to operate the shared national services on which the whole system depends: the identity and demographic spine, the messaging infrastructure, the electronic prescription service, the electronic referral service, the citizen application and the national data platforms. These are critical national infrastructure whose availability is a clinical safety property, and their operation is substantially delivered through long-running supplier arrangements, so supplier management is operational management of national infrastructure rather than a procurement activity.

property.value: National digital functions in transition; suppliers

element.name: Spine and Core National Services
element.documentation: Operating the demographic service, the identity spine and the core messaging infrastructure that most other national services depend upon.

element.name: National Transactional Service Operation
element.documentation: Operating the electronic prescription and electronic referral services, which are among the few genuinely national end-to-end transactional flows.

element.name: Citizen Service Operation
element.documentation: Operating the citizen application, login and website through which people access services and their own record.

element.name: Platform and Infrastructure Operation
element.documentation: Providing hosting, network and platform services including the national network and cloud arrangements on which national and local services run.

element.name: Interoperability and Information Sharing
element.documentation: The ability to move information between independently procured systems and organisations. Realised through a mixture of generations: legacy messaging still carrying high volumes, a national primary care interoperability interface, resource-based interfaces in newer services, document sharing through shared care records, and secure email carrying everything for which no structured channel exists. Interoperability here is not solved by adding interfaces, because the missing property is shared state and closed loops rather than connectivity.

property.value: National digital functions; ICBs; providers; suppliers; standards bodies

element.name: Messaging and Transfer Services
element.documentation: Operating national messaging, record transfer between practices and secure email. Secure email is architecturally significant precisely because it substitutes for missing structured channels.

element.name: Primary Care Interoperability Interfaces
element.documentation: Providing structured access to primary care record data for other services, under supplier assurance rather than ownership.

property.value: National digital functions; primary care system suppliers

element.name: Shared Care Record Operation
element.documentation: Assembling a read-only view across local organisations. Makes the reconstructed longitudinal view persist and be shared without making the underlying record shared or writable.

element.name: Interface Assurance and Onboarding
element.documentation: Assuring and connecting systems to national services, including the compliance regimes that are the principal lever over software the enterprise does not procure.

element.name: Identity and Access Management
element.documentation: The ability to know who a person is and who a user is, and to control what each may see. The national number and demographic service give the system something most comparable health systems lack: a single person identifier used across the estate. Workforce identity and access are less unified, with smartcard-based authentication for national services coexisting with per-system local access control, so an enterprise view of who can see what does not exist and access recertification is performed system by system.

element.name: Person Identification and Demographic Services
element.documentation: Allocating and resolving the national number and maintaining demographic data used across the estate. The load-bearing dependency for every national aggregation.

element.name: Workforce Authentication and Authorisation

The architecture is moving from data dissemination toward access within secure data environments, which changes the governance model fundamentally: analysts come to the data rather than the data going to analysts. element.documentation: The ability to protect the estate from attack and to continue operating when it fails. The system has direct experience of both a national ransomware event affecting clinical services and supplier compromises disrupting pathology and other services, which has made supply chain risk a first-order concern rather than a technical one. The recurring difficulty is that learning is generated nationally and must be implemented in hundreds of autonomous organisations, so the gap between a recommendation and a change in practice is the principal safety architecture problem rather than the detection of harm itself.

The current transition involves dissolving the national body into the department, halving the combined national headcount, converting regional teams into departmental outposts, reducing commissioner running costs and merging integrated care board footprints, all concurrently. The architectural risk is not the destination but the concurrency: capabilities that depend on institutional memory and on relationships between named individuals degrade faster than organisation charts suggest.

element.name: Stay Well

element.name: Get Help When Something Is Wrong
element.documentation: Receiving a request for help through any channel, assessing it and directing it to the right service. Spans digital and telephone triage, primary care access and emergency presentation, and is the stream where the public most often experiences the system as fragmented.

element.name: Get Diagnosed
element.documentation: Converting a clinical question into a diagnosis through assessment, testing and specialist opinion. The stream where waiting is most consequential clinically and where capacity constraints in diagnostics and reporting bite hardest.

element.name: Get Treated
element.documentation: Delivering the therapeutic intervention, whether surgical, medical, psychological or pharmaceutical, in the setting appropriate to need. The stream carrying the largest share of cost and the most visible waiting measure.

element.name: Recover and Stay Independent
element.documentation: Rehabilitation, reablement and support to return to and remain in the community after illness or admission. Depends on joint health and social care capacity that no single organisation controls, which is why it manifests as delayed discharge rather than as a recognisable service failure.

element.name: Live With a Long-Term Condition
element.documentation: Continuing management of chronic illness through recall, review, self-management support and coordinated care. Predominantly a primary care and community stream, measured largely through incentive scheme indicators rather than through outcomes.

element.name: Begin Life and Grow Up
element.documentation: Maternity, neonatal, child health and children's mental health care through to transition into adult services. Distinctive in being surveillance over years rather than episodes, and in changing provider, record and threshold at an age boundary.

element.name: Approach the End of Life
element.documentation: Palliative and end of life care across settings, including advance care planning and coordination of the person's expressed wishes. The stream most dependent on information following a person between organisations out of hours, and therefore the clearest test of whether shared records work in practice.

element.name: Patient Pathway Processes
