element.name: Person, Identity and Consent
element.documentation: The concepts by which the enterprise knows who someone is and what they have agreed to. England's structural advantage over most comparable systems is here: a single person identifier used across the estate.

element.name: Care Delivery
element.documentation: The shape of care: referrals, appointments, pathways, episodes and transfers. Held institutionally, so the person's course of care is a set of separately held records associated by identifier rather than a single object.

element.name: Clinical Content
element.documentation: What was found, decided and done. Divides into a coded core that travels and a narrative body that carries the decisive meaning and travels poorly.

element.name: Diagnostics
element.documentation: Requests, results, images and genomic findings. The domain with the most mature machine-to-machine flows and the clearest illustration of the difference between transmission and retrieval.

element.name: Medicines and Immunisation
element.documentation: Prescribing, dispensing, the current medication picture and vaccination. Primary care prescribing is one of the few genuinely national end-to-end digital flows.

element.name: Population and Public Health
element.documentation: Programme and population constructs: screening, notification, cohorts and inequality measures. Separately governed and derived from registration rather than from clinical systems.

element.name: Workforce, Organisation and Asset
element.documentation: Who delivers care, under which organisation, where and with what. Substantially reference data on which the rest of the model depends, and currently subject to structural change.

element.name: Commissioning and Finance
element.documentation: Contracts, allocations, reported activity, payment and cost. The commissioning dataset is the join between clinical activity and money, and it is retrospective by construction.

element.name: Governance and Assurance
element.documentation: Safety incidents, complaints, regulatory findings, indicators, audit and risk. How the enterprise sees and accounts for itself.

element.name: Metadata and Semantics
element.documentation: Definitions, terminology, provenance and quality. In a federated estate these must be explicit, and they are the layer on which national comparability entirely depends.

element.name: NHS Number
element.documentation: The single national person identifier, allocated at birth or on first contact and used across the estate. A genuine structural advantage compared with health systems that must match on demographics alone. It is a national key rather than a national record, so it enables linkage without conferring a shared view, and matching quality remains the load-bearing dependency for every national aggregation.

element.name: Patient
element.documentation: The person as represented in a provider's systems. Registered separately in each organisation, so the concept exists as multiple representations associated by identifier. The most complete longitudinal clinical account sits in the registered practice record, held by an independent contractor.

property.value: Every provider organisation; the practice record as de facto longitudinal holder

element.name: Person Demographics
element.documentation: Name, date of birth, address, contact details and death notification, maintained nationally and consumed widely. Address quality determines whether invitations, results and correspondence reach the person at all, which makes it a clinical concern as well as an administrative one.

element.name: Registered Patient List Entry
element.documentation: The registration relationship between a person and a practice. The denominator for capitation, incentive schemes, screening invitation and most population accountability, which makes list accuracy a systemic dependency rather than a local housekeeping matter.

element.name: Citizen Account and Verified Identity
element.documentation: The verified digital identity through which a person accesses their record and transacts with services. The level of verification achieved determines what may be exposed, so identity assurance is a gate on the whole citizen-facing architecture.

element.name: Consent and National Data Opt-Out
element.documentation: The person's expressed preferences, including the national opt-out honoured across secondary uses. Notable for being one of the few consent constructs in any health system that is operationally applied at national scale rather than recorded and then ignored.

element.name: Reasonable Adjustment and Communication Need
element.documentation: Recorded needs requiring adjustment to how care is delivered or communicated. Nationally flagged in principle and inconsistently acted upon in practice, which is a recognised equality and safety gap.

element.name: Carer and Next of Kin
element.documentation: The people around the person who receive information, support care and hold context. Weakly represented in systems relative to the operational weight they carry, particularly at discharge and at end of life.

element.name: Referral
element.documentation: A request for specialist assessment or care. A one-way snapshot that freezes the referrer's account, with triage outcome returning inconsistently, so the referrer does not reliably learn what happened.

property.value: Originating system; transmitted; held by receiver

element.name: Appointment
element.documentation: A scheduled contact. Plural across systems and aggregated for the citizen view, which makes it an instructive case of aggregation without integration.

property.value: Provider and practice scheduling systems; surfaced to citizens

element.name: Waiting List Entry and Pathway Clock
element.documentation: A person's position and elapsed time on a pathway. The clock start and stop are information events with substantial political and operational consequence, and validation practice materially affects the reported national position.

element.name: Encounter and Attendance
element.documentation: A single contact between a person and a service. The finest-grained unit at which activity is reliably recorded and the anchor to which most clinical content attaches.

element.name: Hospital Spell and Episode
element.documentation: The structure of an admission, divided into consultant episodes. The unit on which admitted patient care reporting, coding and payment are built.

element.name: Care Plan
element.documentation: The intended course of care. Conceptually central and architecturally homeless: no shared plan is read from and written to by all parties, so coordination proceeds by correspondence and conversation.

property.value: Held within the record of whoever authored it

element.name: Assessment
element.documentation: A structured professional judgement of need or risk, performed under several different statutory regimes. Frequently re-created rather than retrieved when a person re-enters a service.

property.value: Provider, community and local authority systems

element.name: Discharge Summary
element.documentation: The condensation of an admission into a document. For everyone outside the discharging organisation this is the meaning of the admission, and structured medication becomes narrative in the process.

property.value: Discharging provider; received by primary care

element.name: Transfer of Care Event
element.documentation: The moment clinical responsibility moves between teams or organisations. Where responsibility changes hands while the systems hand nothing on with it.

element.name: Care Team Assignment
element.documentation: Who is responsible for coordinating a person's care. Recorded locally, and its loss on staff change is a recognised source of continuity failure in long-running cases.

element.name: Clinical Observation
element.documentation: A measured or recorded clinical fact. Structured at source and among the best data the enterprise creates, and it generally does not leave the originating system in structured form.

property.value: Clinical, nursing, device and laboratory systems

element.name: Coded Diagnosis
element.documentation: The clinical conclusion, expressed clinically by the treating team and separately and retrospectively in a classification by coders for payment and statistics. The two are reconciled statistically rather than transactionally.

element.name: Coded Procedure
element.documentation: An intervention performed, coded retrospectively. A principal driver of payment and of comparative activity reporting, and much less consistently captured outside the acute setting.

element.name: Problem and Condition List
element.documentation: The current and past conditions attributed to a person. Best maintained in primary care and not authoritative anywhere else, which is why other settings re-elicit it.

element.name: Allergy and Adverse Reaction
element.documentation: One of the few clinical facts that must be known everywhere and is recorded everywhere separately, with no authoritative national statement. A standing safety exposure of the same kind as the unreconciled medication list.

element.name: Clinical Document and Correspondence
element.documentation: The letter, summary or report carrying meaning across boundaries. Provenance attaches to the document and its author rather than to each fact within it, and the chain collapses toward the most recent author with each re-narration.

property.value: Created at source; transmitted; filed by receiver

element.name: Risk Assessment
element.documentation: A classification determining care intensity, provisional by design and expected to change. The architecture holds the current value rather than the versioned trajectory.

property.value: Mental health, maternity, safeguarding and community services

element.name: Advance Care Plan and Treatment Escalation Decision
element.documentation: The person's recorded wishes about future care and escalation. Its value is entirely a function of whether an unfamiliar service can retrieve it quickly out of hours, which makes it the sharpest practical test of shared record deployment.

property.value: Primary care; shared care records; ambulance access

element.name: Diagnostic Request
element.documentation: The order linking a clinical question to an investigation. Where order communications are absent, the link between indication and result is weak and closed-loop tracking is local rather than systemic.

element.name: Pathology Result
element.documentation: A validated laboratory result. Delivered to a requester rather than held in common, so comparability depends on local codes and reference ranges that pathology networking is standardising.

property.value: Laboratory information systems; delivered by message

element.name: Imaging Study and Report
element.documentation: Acquired images and their narrative interpretation. Behaves as a shared asset where network archives exist and as a transmitted artefact where they do not, and clinicians experience the difference immediately.

property.value: Provider archives; imaging network sharing arrangements

element.name: Genomic Test Result
element.documentation: Variant findings and their interpretation against a national test directory. Volume and interpretive complexity both growing faster than the clinical record's ability to carry them.

element.name: Prescription
element.documentation: The instruction to supply. Structured and transmitted electronically end to end in primary care, which is unusual internationally, and considerably weaker across the hospital boundary.

element.name: Dispensing Event
element.documentation: What was actually supplied. A more accurate account of what the person received than the prescriber's record of what was intended.

property.value: Community and hospital pharmacy systems; reimbursement processing

element.name: Medication List
element.documentation: The current medication picture. Best held in the practice record and rebuilt by hand at each transition, because no system holds an authoritative statement that all parties read.

property.value: Primary care record; reconciled manually at transitions

element.name: Vaccination Record
element.documentation: Vaccination as a discrete codeable event. Among the most structured clinical data in existence and distributed across several national and local sources, so a complete history requires reconciliation.

property.value: Practice systems; national immunisation services; school services

element.name: Screening Invitation and Result
element.documentation: The invitation, result and recall position for a programme. The failsafe loop connecting them is closed inside the programme rather than across the wider system.

element.name: Notifiable Disease Notification
element.documentation: A statutory notification with defined timelines. Crosses a statutory organisational boundary at the point where speed matters most.

property.value: Clinicians and laboratories; national health protection agency

element.name: Population Segment and Cohort
element.documentation: A group defined by need or risk for whom an offer is designed. Methodologically variable between systems, which limits comparison of the interventions built on it.

property.value: Secure data environments; ICB and network analytics

element.name: Health Inequality Measure
element.documentation: A measure of differential access, experience or outcome between groups. The measure against which the enterprise's principal stated policy purpose is judged.

element.name: Healthcare Professional
element.documentation: The clinician as an actor in the record and a user of systems. Professional registration is held by independent regulators, so the enterprise consults registers it does not own.

property.value: Provider systems; professional regulators; national identity services

element.name: Workforce Record
element.documentation: The employment record and its establishment, cost and deployment attributes. Substantially national in England, which is unusual, and currently subject to large-scale change at the centre.

property.value: National electronic staff record; provider HR

element.name: Organisation and Site Reference Data
element.documentation: The authoritative register of organisations, sites and their codes. Load-bearing for routing, payment and reporting, and being re-expressed as integrated care board boundaries change, which is a recurring source of historical comparability problems.

element.name: Service and Directory Entry
element.documentation: The catalogue of services available and how to reach them. Routing failures are directory failures, which makes this considerably more consequential than its subject matter suggests.

element.name: Estate and Facility
element.documentation: Buildings, their condition and their capacity. Backlog maintenance is a material constraint on both clinical productivity and digital deployment.

element.name: Medical Device and Equipment
element.documentation: Equipment generating or holding clinical data. Both a data source and a vulnerability surface, since legacy platforms persist where they are tied to clinical equipment.

element.name: Contract
element.documentation: The instrument allocating scope, funding and obligation, from the national standard contract to independent contractor agreements. The principal lever the enterprise holds over delivery it does not manage.

element.name: Commissioning Dataset Record
element.documentation: The submitted record of activity used for payment, statistics and oversight. The join between clinical activity and money, retrospective by construction and definitionally governed nationally.

element.name: Allocation and Budget
element.documentation: The distributed settlement and the envelopes derived from it. Allocation is weighted by population need and attaches to organisations rather than to episodes of care.

element.name: Payment and Reconciliation Record
element.documentation: What was paid and against what. Mixes block, aligned and activity-based elements, so the relationship to delivery is indirect and reconciled after the event.

element.name: Patient-Level Cost Record
element.documentation: Resource consumption attributed to individual patients. Sophisticated, nationally collected, and used less operationally than its quality would justify because it arrives late.

element.name: Activity Plan and Trajectory
element.documentation: The planned volume and profile of activity against which delivery is monitored. The instrument by which national objectives become local commitments.

element.name: Patient Safety Incident Record
element.documentation: A recorded incident or near miss and the response to it. Very high volume nationally, with the constraint being translation into practice change rather than detection.

element.name: Complaint, Feedback and Experience Response
element.documentation: What people say about their care. A significant source of signal about coordination failures that operational data does not show, and used less than it could be because it arrives as narrative.

element.name: Regulatory Rating and Inspection Finding
element.documentation: The regulator's published judgement. Independent of the commissioning oversight line, so a provider may be judged differently by each, and reconciling the two is a routine board task.

element.name: Performance Indicator
element.documentation: The measures by which the system accounts for itself, many with official statistics status. Strong within domains and difficult across a pathway, so the enterprise reports what each part did more readily than what happened to a person.

property.value: National statistics and oversight functions; providers

element.name: Audit Record
element.documentation: Who accessed what and when. Held per system and not aggregated, so cross-system investigation is manual and an enterprise view of access does not exist.

element.name: Information Standard
element.documentation: A published standard with a compliance date, issued through a statutory process. The mechanism by which national coherence is imposed on locally procured systems.

element.name: Data Access Agreement
element.documentation: The terms on which data may be used and by whom. Increasingly attached to access within a controlled environment rather than to a transfer of data.

property.value: National data functions; access committees; researchers

element.name: Risk Register Entry
element.documentation: A recorded risk with owner and mitigation. Enterprise-level risk is dominated by dependencies the enterprise does not wholly control, including suppliers, social care capacity and its own restructure.

element.name: Terminology and Code System
element.documentation: The clinical terminology, the medicines dictionary and the classifications used for coding activity. England mandates a single clinical terminology across the estate, which is a stronger semantic position than most national systems achieve.

element.name: Data Dictionary Definition
element.documentation: The definition of a data item, its permitted values and its provenance. The authority that makes national aggregation of locally held data meaningful.

element.name: Provenance and Lineage
element.documentation: Where a fact came from and how it was transformed. Handled well inside platforms and poorly across them, which is the characteristic weakness of federated estates.

property.value: Implicit within platforms; largely absent between them

element.name: Data Quality Measure
element.documentation: Measured fitness for purpose, including submission completeness and identifier matching rates. Identifier quality is the highest-leverage measure because its effects are systemic.

element.name: Citizens and Their Representatives
element.documentation: The people the system exists for, and the bodies that represent them. In this architecture they also perform work: carrying their own history between organisations that do not exchange it.

element.name: The Clinical and Care Workforce
element.documentation: Those who deliver care and perform the human integration the systems do not. The largest cost in the system and its principal capacity constraint.

element.name: Delivery Organisations
element.documentation: The autonomous statutory and independent bodies that actually provide and commission care. The centre influences them through contract, standard, payment and inspection rather than through line management.

element.name: National Bodies and Regulators
element.documentation: The departmental, arm's-length and regulatory tier. Currently the part of the architecture undergoing the most structural change.

element.name: Suppliers, Academia and Partners
element.documentation: Those who build, run and study the estate. Much of the enterprise's operational digital capability is exercised through third parties.

element.name: Patients and Citizens
element.documentation: Recipients of care and, at every boundary the systems do not bridge, the carriers of their own information. Increasingly transacting directly through national digital channels, which makes the completeness of what those channels can show a matter of public visibility rather than internal concern.

element.name: Carers and Families
element.documentation: Hold and carry context for those who cannot, and perform coordination the architecture does not, most visibly at discharge, in end of life care and for children and people with complex needs. Load-bearing and weakly represented in systems.

element.name: Healthwatch and Patient Representative Bodies
element.documentation: Independent statutory and voluntary bodies representing the public voice in service planning, scrutiny and complaint. The route by which experience becomes a formal input to commissioning rather than anecdote.

element.name: Doctors
element.documentation: Make the consequential clinical decisions across primary, secondary and specialist care. In primary care they are frequently also contract holders and business owners, which makes them commercial counterparties as well as clinicians and is central to how change reaches general practice.

element.name: Nurses, Midwives and Health Visitors
element.documentation: The largest professional group, delivering and coordinating care across every setting and holding continuity through episodes that several doctors may pass through.

element.name: Allied Health Professionals
element.documentation: Therapy, diagnostic and rehabilitation professions across acute and community settings. Their assessment data is highly structured at source and largely invisible to the rest of the system.

element.name: Pharmacists and Pharmacy Teams
element.documentation: Supply, clinical check, reconciliation and an expanding set of clinical services under the community pharmacy contract. The profession most affected by the shift of clinical activity out of general practice.

element.name: Ambulance Clinicians
element.documentation: Assess and treat at scene and in transit, and decide whether to convey. Their clinical record reaches the receiving hospital inconsistently, so their assessment is frequently reduced to a verbal handover.

element.name: Social Care Workforce
element.documentation: Employed by local authorities and independent providers under separate statutory accountability and separate funding. Not part of the NHS and indispensable to its flow, which is the defining feature of the discharge interface.

element.name: NHS Trusts and Foundation Trusts
element.documentation: Autonomous statutory providers of acute, community, mental health and ambulance services, with their own boards and, for foundation trusts, additional freedoms. They hold the clinical record estate and the majority of the workforce.

element.name: Integrated Care Boards
element.documentation: Statutory commissioners responsible for planning and buying services for a population, working with local government through integrated care partnerships. Their footprints changed in April 2026 with further change due, and their running costs are being substantially reduced, so their capacity to exercise strategic commissioning is contracting as their populations grow.

element.name: Primary Medical Care Contractors
element.documentation: Independent businesses holding contracts to provide primary medical services to a registered list, using clinical systems the NHS does not own. The most complete longitudinal record of the population sits here, and change reaches this stakeholder through contract negotiation rather than direction.

element.name: Community Pharmacy Contractors
element.documentation: Independent contractors dispensing medicines and delivering an expanding clinical service set. Connected to the national prescription infrastructure, which makes this one of the better integrated independent sectors.

element.name: Independent Sector Providers
element.documentation: Deliver elective, diagnostic and mental health capacity under NHS contract at significant scale. Activity reports into national datasets while the underlying clinical record remains outside the NHS estate, so episodes return as correspondence.

element.name: Local Authorities
element.documentation: Statutory responsibility for adult and children's social care and for public health, with democratic accountability the NHS does not have. Partner in every integrated arrangement and subordinate in none, and the counterparty at the system's highest-friction interface.

element.name: Voluntary and Community Sector
element.documentation: Deliver services, advocacy and support under grant and contract, frequently reaching populations statutory services do not. Digital maturity varies widely and information flow to NHS records is rarely integrated.

element.name: Department of Health and Social Care
element.documentation: Sets policy, secures and distributes the settlement, and accounts to Parliament. Currently absorbing the functions of the national body, with the new departmental centre expected to operate from 2027 and regional teams becoming departmental outposts. Accountability is therefore moving closer to ministers.

element.name: NHS England (in transition)
element.documentation: The national body being wound down into the department: commissioner of specialised and primary care services, operator of national digital services, publisher of standards and holder of the oversight framework. Its abolition was announced in March 2025 and requires legislation; the practical consequence for this model is that many capabilities are recorded against an organisation that will not hold them for long.

element.name: UK Health Security Agency
element.documentation: Separate national agency for health protection, surveillance and outbreak response. Holds a capability the NHS depends on across a statutory organisational boundary, which is where the flow is slowest at the moment speed matters most.

element.name: Care Quality Commission
element.documentation: Independent regulator registering, inspecting and rating providers against fundamental standards. Independent of the commissioning oversight line, so its judgement and system oversight may diverge.

element.name: NICE and Assessment Bodies
element.documentation: Assess technologies and produce guidance, with mandated funding requirements attaching to some decisions. One of the few mechanisms by which a national decision reaches prescribing and treatment directly.

element.name: MHRA and Professional Regulators
element.documentation: Regulate medicines, devices and software as a medical device, and register and revalidate professionals. The enterprise consults workforce registers it does not own and deploys software subject to regulation it does not administer.

element.name: Information Commissioner and National Data Guardian
element.documentation: Independent oversight of data protection and of the use of health and care information. The institutional expression of the principle that public trust is an architectural constraint rather than a communications matter.

element.name: Clinical System Suppliers
element.documentation: Provide the electronic patient record, primary care and departmental systems in which care is recorded. Market concentration in primary care is high, and the enterprise's influence runs through assurance and framework compliance rather than ownership.

element.name: National Service and Infrastructure Suppliers
element.documentation: Operate national digital services, hosting and network under long-running contracts. Supplier management here is operational management of critical national infrastructure, and supplier compromise has directly disrupted clinical services.

element.name: Academia and Research Networks
element.documentation: Universities, clinical research networks and life sciences partners using NHS data and settings. Depend directly on the data and information governance capabilities, and constitute one of the enterprise's genuine international advantages.

element.name: National Core Digital Services
element.documentation: The shared national services on which the whole estate depends. England's set is unusually extensive by international comparison and is now inside an organisation being dissolved, which places continuity of critical national infrastructure on the transition risk register.

element.name: Interoperability and Messaging Services
element.documentation: The mechanisms moving information between independently procured systems. Several generations operate simultaneously, and secure email persists as the universal fallback wherever a structured channel is absent.

element.name: Primary Care Systems
element.documentation: The clinical systems of independent contractors, holding the most complete longitudinal record of the population in software the NHS does not own and influences through assurance and framework compliance.

element.name: Provider Clinical and Administrative Systems
element.documentation: The locally procured electronic record, administrative and departmental systems in which the majority of clinical activity is recorded. Heterogeneous by construction and the reason national aggregation is a collection exercise.

element.name: Shared Record and Citizen Services
element.documentation: The layer assembling views across organisations and exposing them to clinicians and to citizens. Aggregation rather than integration: it makes the reconstructed longitudinal view persist without making the underlying record shared or writable.

element.name: Data, Analytics and Secure Environments
element.documentation: National collection, linkage, analysis and publication, moving from dissemination toward governed access within controlled environments.

element.name: Corporate and Back Office Systems
element.documentation: Workforce, finance, procurement and supply chain. More nationally consolidated than the clinical estate, which produces the familiar asymmetry between canonical money and assembled activity.

element.name: Identity, Access and Security Services
element.documentation: Authentication, authorisation, monitoring and network protection across national services and provider estates.

element.name: Personal Demographics Service
element.documentation: The national demographic and identity service holding person records against the national number and distributing updates to consuming systems. The single most architecturally load-bearing national service, because everything else assumes it.

element.name: Spine Core Messaging and Services
element.documentation: The core national messaging and service infrastructure through which national transactions and demographic updates flow. Critical national infrastructure whose availability is a clinical safety property.

element.name: Electronic Prescription Service
element.documentation: National transmission of prescriptions from prescriber to dispenser and on to reimbursement. One of the few genuinely national end-to-end digital flows and a correspondingly rich national dataset.

element.name: NHS e-Referral Service
element.documentation: Directory-based referral, slot publication and booking for consultant-led services, including patient-initiated booking. Carries most elective referral and starts the pathway clock.

element.name: NHS App and NHS Login
element.documentation: The national citizen channel and its identity verification. An aggregation layer, so what a citizen sees of themselves reflects the architecture behind it including where it is incomplete.

element.name: NHS Website and Service Finder
element.documentation: Public information about conditions and services, and the directory used to locate them. The most used health information source in the country and the front of the navigation architecture.

element.name: Directory of Services
element.documentation: The authoritative catalogue of services and their availability used to route urgent care dispositions. Routing failures are directory failures, which makes its currency a clinical matter.

element.name: Organisation Data Service
element.documentation: National reference data for organisations, sites and their codes. Being re-expressed as integrated care board boundaries change, which is a recurring source of historical comparability problems in reporting.

element.name: National Immunisation and Vaccination Services
element.documentation: National recording and call and recall for vaccination programmes, operating alongside practice systems and school age services so that a complete history requires reconciliation.

element.name: National Screening Call and Recall Services
element.documentation: Population registers, invitation, result management and failsafe recall for the national screening programmes, derived from registration data rather than from clinical systems.

element.name: Message Exchange and National Messaging
element.documentation: Store and forward messaging between organisations and national services, carrying high volumes of administrative and clinical traffic including dataset submissions.

element.name: GP Connect and Primary Care Interoperability Interfaces
element.documentation: Structured access to primary care record data for other services, delivered by independent suppliers under assurance rather than ownership. The principal route by which the richest clinical record in the system becomes readable elsewhere.

element.name: Practice Record Transfer Service
element.documentation: Structured transfer of the electronic patient record between practices on registration change. Unusual internationally, and the record is nevertheless re-based on transfer.

element.name: NHSmail and Secure Email
element.documentation: Secure correspondence between organisations. Architecturally significant precisely because it substitutes for missing structured channels, and its prevalence measures where structured integration does not reach.

element.name: GP Clinical Systems
element.documentation: The clinical systems of independent primary medical contractors, holding registration, consultation, problem list, prescribing and long-term condition data. Market concentration is high and the enterprise influences them through assurance and framework compliance.

element.name: Online Consultation and Digital Triage Tools
element.documentation: Systems receiving and triaging requests submitted online, now central to how primary care manages total demand across channels.

element.name: Electronic Patient Record Systems
element.documentation: Provider clinical record systems, procured locally with varying maturity. The largest single determinant of what data a provider can produce and therefore of what the national estate can see.

element.name: Patient Administration Systems
element.documentation: Registration, admission, transfer, discharge, scheduling and waiting list management. The de facto administrative spine of a provider and the source of most reported activity.

element.name: Laboratory Information Systems
element.documentation: Specimen receipt, analysis, validation and reporting across networked laboratories, with local codes and reference ranges that pathology networking is progressively standardising.

element.name: Radiology Systems and Image Archives
element.documentation: Imaging acquisition, reporting, storage and network sharing. Behaves as a retrieval capability where shared archives exist and a transmission capability where they do not.

element.name: Electronic Prescribing and Medicines Administration
element.documentation: Inpatient prescribing and administration. Deployment is uneven, and where it is absent the hospital medicines record remains paper and the discharge summary carries medication as narrative.

element.name: Emergency Department and Ambulance Systems
element.documentation: Registration, triage, tracking and pre-hospital clinical records. The pre-hospital record reaches the receiving system inconsistently, so handover remains substantially verbal.

element.name: Mental Health and Community Information Systems
element.documentation: Records for mental health and community services, including Mental Health Act administration. Predominantly narrative content and materially less complete national reporting than acute equivalents.

element.name: Shared Care Records
element.documentation: Read-only assembly of information across local organisations for clinicians. Makes the reconstructed longitudinal view persist and be shared without making the underlying record shared or writable, which is the precise boundary of what aggregation achieves.

element.name: Summary and Shared Record National Services
element.documentation: National summary record services making core primary care information available to unscheduled care. The longest-standing national shared record capability and deliberately limited in scope.

element.name: Secondary Uses Service and National Collections
element.documentation: National collection and curation of commissioning datasets underpinning payment, statistics and oversight. The join between clinical activity and money, and retrospective by construction.

element.name: Federated Data Platform and Operational Analytics
element.documentation: Shared platform and analytics capability offered to systems and providers for operational use, including flow and elective coordination. Notable for placing national platform capability directly into provider operations rather than only into national reporting.

element.name: Secure Data Environments
element.documentation: Governed analytic access to linked data within controlled environments rather than by dissemination. Changes the governance question from who may hold data to who may work with it and under what supervision.

element.name: National Statistics Publication Services
element.documentation: Production and publication of official statistics to defined standards and timetables, which constrains definitional change elsewhere in the architecture.

element.name: Electronic Staff Record
element.documentation: The national workforce and payroll system used across the provider estate. Unusually consolidated by international standards, and the source of national workforce statistics.

element.name: Finance and Ledger Systems
element.documentation: Provider and commissioner ledgers and the national collections consolidating them. More nationally coherent than the clinical estate, which produces the asymmetry between canonical money and assembled activity.

element.name: Supply Chain and Procurement Systems
element.documentation: National supply chain and procurement platforms alongside local inventory management. Aggregate spend visibility exceeds consumption visibility at the point of use.

element.name: Contractor Payment and Reimbursement Services
element.documentation: Payment of independent primary care and pharmacy contractors including incentive scheme achievement. A by-product is one of the better sources of structured primary care data available nationally.

element.name: Care Identity and Smartcard Services
element.documentation: Workforce authentication and role-based authorisation for national services, coexisting with per-system local access control in provider estates. An enterprise view of who can see what does not exist.

element.name: National Cyber Operations and Network Protection
element.documentation: Monitoring, detection and protective services across the national network and provider estates, including supplier assurance following incidents in which supplier compromise disrupted clinical delivery.

element.name: National Patient Safety Learning Services
element.documentation: National recording of patient safety events and the generation of learning and alerts from them. Very high volume, with translation into practice change the binding constraint.
